terms.meaning: The path that devotion is the best way to Moksha, with brotherhood for all.
From "Saaf", meaning clean. Sufi saints were Muslims in plain woollen dress.
A two-line poem; Kabir taught through them.
The window at Udupi through which Krishna is said to have turned to give Kanakadasa darshana.
An important Sufi order founded by Moyinuddin Chisthi of Ajmer.

items.name: What the Bhakthi saints taught
items.formula: Equality, no caste discrimination, no superstition, uniting people's hearts.
items.example: They wrote in simple local languages, which enriched them.

items.name: What the Sufis taught
items.formula: One God, all are his children and equal; love and service is dharma.
items.example: Sufism came from Arabia and later absorbed Yoga, Vedanta and Buddhist ideas.

items.name: Aandal
items.formula: One of the twelve Alwars; original name Godadevi; adopted daughter of Periyalwar.
items.example: She wrote Thirupaavai, loving Krishna as her husband.

items.name: Akkamahadevi
items.formula: Born at Uduthadi (Shivamogga); left King Koushika's palace; wrote vachanas as "Channamallikarjuna".
items.example: She stayed at Basaveshwara's Anubhava Mantapa and died in the Kadali forest of Srishaila.

items.name: Purandaradasa (1480-1564)
items.formula: Born Srinivasa Nayaka, a miser who gave away his wealth; Vyasaraya named him Purandara.
items.example: Pen name "Purandara Vittala"; called Karnataka Sangeetha Pithamaha.

items.name: Kanakadasa (1508-1606)
items.formula: Born Thimmappa at Bada (Haveri), a warrior chief; disciple of Vyasaraya; pen name "Adikeshava".
items.example: Works: Haribhakthisara, Nalacharithre, Ramadhanya Charithe, Mohana Tarangini.

items.name: Shishunala Sharifa
items.formula: Born in 1819 at Shishunala; first Kannada Muslim poet, called the "Kabeera of Karnataka".
items.example: A disciple of Govindabhatta, he wrote Thathvapadas across caste and religion.

items.name: Kabirdas
items.formula: Disciple of Ramananda, raised by the weavers Neeru and Neema of Varanasi.
items.example: Allah and Rama are one God; Hindus and Muslims are pots of the same clay. His followers: Kabir Panthis.

items.name: Gurunanak (1469-1539)
items.formula: Founder of Sikhism, born at Talvandi (now Pakistan); his Japji is in the Grantha Sahib.
items.example: He opposed idol worship, caste and Sati; "Naanak Jhara" at Bidar marks his visit.

items.name: Tulasidas (1532-1623)
items.formula: Devotee of Rama who wrote Ramacharithamanasa in Hindi.
items.example: In the North it is called Tulasiramayana.

items.name: Chaithanya (1485-1533)
items.formula: Born Vishwambara at Navadweep (Bengal); took Sanyasa at 25.
items.example: Bengalis call him Chaithanya Mahaprabhu; the Hare Krishna movement follows him.

items.name: Meerabai (1498-1569)
items.formula: A Rajput princess married into Mewar, called "Kaliyuga's Radha".
items.example: Her favourite deity was Giridhara Gopala.

items.name: Nizamuddin Auliya
items.formula: A Delhi Sufi who lived in poverty and refused a village gifted by the Sultan.
items.example: He preached kindness to all who came.

items.name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz
items.formula: A Chisthi saint of Kalaburagi, also called Gesudaraj ("long haired"); wrote in Dakhani.
items.example: His Urs is held at Kalaburagi every year.

items.name: Sufi saints and their places
items.formula: Ajmer: Moyinuddin Chisthi. Delhi: Nizamuddin Auliya. Kalaburagi: Bande Nawaz. Fatehpur Sikri: Salim Chisthi.

mistakes.text: Pen names: Akka "Channamallikarjuna", Purandara "Purandara Vittala", Kanaka "Adikeshava".
Kabir is a North Indian saint; Shishunala Sharifa is called the Kabir of Karnataka.
"Kaliyuga's Radha" is Meerabai, not Aandal, though both loved Krishna.
